thread:
anya: Heads-up — saw a sharp uptick in funcall parse failures on the int4-canary after we enabled aggressive kv-prefix caching + reduced retry budget. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:
ops-bot: alert: funcall_parse_rate spike 178% in int4-canary (svc=tool-invoke, window=5m)
mike: yup saw it too, started ~1713839800 when the canary rollout toggled cache_mode=aggressive
ian: curious: are the failures malformed JSON, or truncated streams?
anya: mostly truncated/early-eof errors, parsing error: "unexpected end of input" and some extra-commas. looks like outputs getting cut when we double-hit the tool endpoint
sara: could be duplicates due to retry budget exhaustion + liveness probe marking a request dead before full stream flush. we switched retry_budget from 2->1 yesterday to save tokens
ian: that makes sense. if frontend gives up early and resends, tool sees second call and our postprocessor tries to stitch outputs leading to bad tail tokens\mike: grabbing logs from replica A and B. snippet:
```
[2024-04-22T12:03:10Z] req-id=rdw-xyz-12 status=500 reason="kvmiss+timeout"
[2024-04-22T12:03:12Z] req-id=rdw-xyz-12 status=200 tool-response="{\"action\": \"open_file\", \"path\": \"/tmp/x\"\n"
[2024-04-22T12:03:12Z] req-id=rdw-xyz-12 retry=1 forwarded-by=frontend-2
```
mike: note the same req-id got a retry but after the first response started streaming; second arrival truncated the stream on the stitcher
anya: is the frontend deduping by req-id? i thought we set an idempotency header X-Redwood-Invoke-ID but maybe it isn't propagated to the tool shim
sara: config shows X-Redwood-Invoke-ID enabled, but our liveness checker (liveness-serving-probe) uses a synthetic sub-request that doesn't copy headers — so dedupe misses it
ian: two angles: 1) make liveness probe not trigger user-visible retry logic; 2) ensure idempotency header is copied to tool shim and used to reject duplicates during stream assembly
ops-bot: deploy event: rolled out liveness-serving-probe change to int4-canary at 1713840120 by ops (canary-bump 2024-04-22)
anya: quick mitigation idea: bump retry_budget back to 2 for canary and add jittered exponential backoff so we don't hammer tool with immediate duplicates
mike: agreed. also add guard in postprocessor: if we see two streams with same X-Redwood-Invoke-ID, prefer the one that completed a final EOF marker and ignore the earlier partial
sara: propose small change: update liveness probe to use HEAD-only health ping that does not pass through the full invoke path. patch:
```
# liveness config snippet
probe_type: head
pass_headers: []  # do not forward user headers
timeout_ms: 30
```
ian: also add telemetry: emit field "stitch_dropped_partial=true" when we drop a partial stream due to duplicate later arrival. we need metrics to see how often this happens post-fix
anya: i'll open a quick PR for the liveness change + postprocessor guard. can someone run a local chaos run with retry budget=1 and cache_mode=aggressive after the change? want to validate we don't re-introduce token regressions
mike: i'll run a short chaos test (1000 requests, randomized network delay 0-200ms) and post results when done
ops-bot: note: canary-bump paused automatically due to parse_rate alert at 1713840180
canary-bot: canary-health: parse_rate now down to baseline after liveness rollback and retry_budget bump (window=10m)
anya: nice. follow-ups: (1) add idempotency header propagation to tool-shim, (2) metric for dropped-partials, (3) longer-term: evaluate whether aggressive kv-prefix caching is worth this complexity or we need per-request cache affinity
sara: +1 to metrics and idempotency. i'll add a short RFC item for per-request affinity to avoid cross-replica double-hits
ian: FYI add a small prompt-test in our eval harness that forces partial-streams + retries so we catch regressions in CI
mike: posted chaos run summary: 1. baseline parse_fail_rate=0.2% 2. before fix with retry_budget=1 parse_fail_rate=3.8% 3. after liveness HEAD probe + retry_budget=2 parse_fail_rate=0.3% 4. dropped-partials metric reported ~0.6% of requests during window
anya: excellent. i'll keep the canary in watch for 24h then promote if stable. :thumbsup:
